Sound Pest Control sits in Scorpion's book through Coalmarch Marketing (now Scorpion). Scorpion acquired Coalmarch Marketing on 2026-10-19; Coalmarch's pest and lawn client book moved under Scorpion's RevenueMAX platform. Drupal 10 on Pantheon with a shared 'sprowt3' theme and a shared GTM-era analytics pattern; the same build recurs across the pest and lawn book.
The on-page read returned 7 findings (1 High, 3 Medium) and 1 compliance observations; the overall grade is C.
FAQ schema is present and valid on six pages, the raw HTML is server-rendered, and lab LCP is strong.

key_judgments.title: The defects are the agency's template, not the owner's choices
key_judgments.judgment: It is likely that the recurring defects on Sound Pest Control are inherited from the Coalmarch Marketing (now Scorpion) template and platform rather than owned by the business, because The shared sprowt3 Drupal template, the GTM-that-fires-before-any-consent-gate pattern, the Universal-Analytics-id-left-in-container pattern, the Product-schema-on-a-service pattern and the long-title/thin-meta pattern are template-level, so they are inherited from the agency, not owned by the business.
falsifiers: A sibling site on the same template without the same defect would weaken this.
An owner-made change that post-dates the agency build would reassign ownership.

key_judgments.title: The site wins its own name but loses the money searches
key_judgments.judgment: It is very likely that the site captures brand demand but not non-brand demand, because the brand appears in Autocomplete only for its own name while the city+service money terms surface rivals.
falsifiers: A GSC export showing non-brand impressions/clicks at volume would overturn this.
A map-pack screenshot ranking the client for the money terms would overturn this.

key_judgments.title: A challenger can lead with a clean ownership-and-diagnosis contrast
key_judgments.judgment: It is likely that a challenger who leads with a declared audit plus true site ownership can open a conversation, because the lock-in and the inherited defects are public and documented.
falsifiers: A long contract term with heavy exit penalties would lengthen the cycle.
High owner satisfaction despite the defects would weaken the wedge.

findings.title: Sitemap points Google at noindex pages
findings.evidence: 2 URL(s) in the XML sitemap carry a noindex directive, e.g. https://www.soundpestcontrol.com/learning-center. Google wastes crawl budget on pages it is told not to index, and the mixed signal erodes trust in the sitemap.
findings.fix: Either index the page (drop the noindex) or remove it from the sitemap; a sitemap should list only indexable URLs.

findings.title: Sitemap lists a redirecting URL
findings.evidence: The sitemap lists https://www.soundpestcontrol.com/node/12, which 301-redirects. The sitemap should carry only final URLs.
findings.fix: List the destination URL in the sitemap, not the redirecting one.

findings.title: 17 title tags exceed the snippet limit
findings.evidence: 17 crawled pages carry titles over 70 characters, so Google truncates them in results and the city/service keyword can fall off the visible end.
findings.fix: Rewrite titles to ~55-60 characters, front-loading the service and city.

findings.title: LocalBusiness schema omits recommended fields
findings.evidence: The LocalBusiness/▸ markup is missing recommended fields (image, geo, openingHoursSpecification, priceRange, sameAs, areaServed across the audited pages); each raises eligibility for local rich results.
findings.fix: Complete the LocalBusiness block with geo, hours, priceRange, image and sameAs links to the GBP and socials.

findings.title: A dead Universal Analytics id still fires in the container
findings.evidence: The GTM container still loads UA-76032643-1, a Universal Analytics property that Google stopped processing in July 2023. It collects nothing and adds a request and a pre-consent beacon.
findings.fix: Remove the UA tag from the container.

findings.title: Trackers fire before any consent, and there is no consent banner
findings.evidence: On first load, before any interaction, the page fires chat_or_ai_widget, google_ads_doubleclick, google_analytics, google_tag_manager, microsoft_uet with no consent banner anywhere on the site (render probe, 2026-11-15). Consent Mode is present in the container but nothing gates the beacons.
findings.fix: Add a consent banner wired to Google Consent Mode v2 so ad/analytics storage waits for opt-in; at minimum honor GPC and add a privacy choice.

findings.title: Invisible on the money searches; present only on its own name
findings.evidence: In Google Autocomplete the brand appears for 1 of 6 seeds (its own name and close variants) but is absent from the non-brand money terms: pest control tacoma, pest control olympia, rodent control tacoma, pest control puyallup. Answer engines and the map pack reward entities that own the non-brand term; this site owns only its brand.
findings.fix: Win the non-brand terms with complete local entity data, city+service pages and citations; name an AI-crawler posture in robots.txt.

exposure.rule: Trackers firing before consent with no banner
exposure.cite: US state privacy laws (e.g. CPRA/CCPA, CPA) govern sale/share of personal information via ad trackers; a service business can have customers in those states. Not an FTC/GDPR CONFIRMED from a US vantage.
exposure.evidence: Pre-consent beacons: chat_or_ai_widget, google_ads_doubleclick, google_analytics, google_tag_manager, microsoft_uet; no consent banner detected (render probe).
exposure.base_rate: Low enforcement base rate for SMB local sites from a US vantage.
exposure.open_question: Does the business serve California/Colorado/etc. residents, and is any of this data 'sold/shared' under those statutes? An EU banner is not testable from here.
exposure.channel: Client's counsel decides; fix is cheap regardless.

glossary.def: A finding is inherited when it comes from the agency's shared template or platform, owned when the business controls it. It decides who fixes it and who to lead the pitch against.
Ad/analytics tags that run before any consent choice. A privacy exposure under US state laws and GDPR; cheap to fix with a consent banner.
Using schema.org/Product for a service. It has no rich-result path for services and can misdescribe the business to answer engines.
Scorpion's hosting platform. A client site resolving into the scorpcloud CNAME zone is on Scorpion's proprietary CMS - the central lock-in.
A fetch-only run with no client exports. Rankings, traffic and spend are protocols or inferred, not measured.
The intelligence-community probability scale (almost no chance ... almost certain) used so a likelihood word always maps to a number range.
